name: Soft delete and restore
needs: a user removed something by mistake and wants it back
add a trash folder with restore
summary: Marking a record as deleted instead of removing it, so it disappears from the app but can be restored. A purge job removes it for real after a set time, which also matters when someone asks you to erase their data.
need_when: Users delete things they might want back.
Support keeps getting 'I deleted it by accident' requests.
skip_when: The data is cheap to recreate, or must be gone at once for privacy reasons.

ways.title: A deleted_at column and a default filter
ways.how: Add deleted_at, make the default query hide rows where it's set, and keep a separate way to reach all rows for admin and purge.
ways.tradeoff: Simple. Every raw query, join and unique constraint has to remember the filter.

ways.title: A library
ways.how: django-safedelete, Rails' discard gem, or Prisma query extensions.
ways.tradeoff: Less code to write. Learn how it treats related records.

ways.title: Move rows to an archive table
ways.how: On delete, copy the row to a trash table and delete the original. Restore copies it back.
ways.tradeoff: Main queries stay simple. Restoring rows with relations takes more work.

prompt:
Add soft delete with restore to [model].

Requirements:
- Add deleted_at (nullable, indexed). Deleting sets it instead of removing the row.
- The default query everywhere hides deleted rows. Admin and the purge job use an explicit all-rows query.
- Unique constraints only apply to rows that aren't deleted (a partial unique index on Postgres).
- Add a Trash view where the owner can restore items within [30] days.
- A daily job permanently deletes rows that have been in the trash longer than [30] days, including their files.
- An account deletion request skips the trash and removes the data for good.
- Log who deleted and restored what.

Acceptance checks (run each and show me the result):
1. A deleted item disappears from lists, search and the API.
2. Restoring brings it back with its related data.
3. Creating a new item with the same unique name as a deleted one works.
4. After the retention period the purge job removes it and its files.
5. Grep shows no raw queries that skip the deleted filter.
acceptance_checks: A deleted item disappears from lists, search and the API.
Restoring brings it back with its related data.
Creating a new item with the same unique name as a deleted one works.
After the retention period the purge job removes it and its files.
Grep shows no raw queries that skip the deleted filter.
if_you_skip_it: Deleted items come back in search or counts, unique names stay taken forever, or 'deleted' data is still there when someone asks you to erase it.
how_derek_runs_it: Custody Journal's journal entries, custody events and communications share a soft-delete base with is_deleted and an indexed deleted_at. The default manager hides deleted rows, and a separate all_objects manager is used for admin, migrations and purging. Admin actions restore selected items, and soft deletes are written to the audit log.
